items.followUp: State two differences between RAM and a hard drive.

rubric.why: Storage is used to retain data and programs for future use.
rubric.description: Identifies storage as long-term or permanent data retention.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that storage retains data long-term or permanently, or identifying it as secondary storage.

rubric.why: Memory holds data and instructions needed for current processing.
rubric.description: Identifies memory as temporary or used for current processing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that memory is temporary, volatile, or used for current processing.

modelAnswer: Storage keeps data and programs for long-term use, usually on secondary devices such as a hard drive.
Memory holds data and instructions needed for current processing; it is generally temporary.
Therefore, storage is for long-term retention, while memory is used for current processing.
Example: a hard drive is storage; RAM is memory.

items.followUp: Define IPv6 and state the length of its addresses.

rubric.why: IPv4 addresses have a 32-bit length and are divided into four octets.
rubric.description: States the length or four-part structure of an IPv4 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an IPv4 address is 32 bits long or consists of four octets.

rubric.why: A valid example shows the dotted-decimal form of an IPv4 address.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of an IPv4 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid four-part dotted-decimal example.

modelAnswer: IPv4 (Internet Protocol version 4) is an addressing system that uses 32-bit addresses to identify devices on a network.
An IPv4 address is written as four decimal numbers separated by dots; for example, 192.168.1.1.
